clue.text: Confirm Valerie has one assignation

parts.note: Val is the short form of the name Valerie
one is the Roman numeral I
an assignation is a date, an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: Valerie is said to have a single romantic rendezvous lined up.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm something is to make it officially valid or approve it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Prove to be true provided there's light outside

indicators.note: outside says the light's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol
if means provided, on condition that

explanation.surface: A test of truth that depends on light shining outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify a claim is to confirm by evidence that it holds.

clue.text: Learning about a hot place in the east

indicators.note: about means the word for learning goes round the other letters

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge or learning
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Studying around a sweltering spot somewhere in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: This city in Pakistan, capital of Punjab province, lies in South Asia, the East to a British setter.

clue.text: Music from in France barely sufficient

parts.note: de is French for from
scant means barely enough

explanation.surface: French music that is only just adequate.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a melody sung or played above the main tune, a type of music.

clue.text: Dry man, does he count all the holes, except the nineteenth, of course?

definitions.meaning: a man who drinks no alcohol, dry in the sense of abstaining

definitions.text: does he count all the holes, except the nineteenth, of course?
definitions.meaning: the nineteenth hole is golfers' slang for the clubhouse bar

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into TEE and TOTALLER: one who totals the tees. The 'nineteenth hole' is golfing slang for the bar, which an abstainer would skip.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer who never touches alcohol is described as dry, the joke of the clue.

clue.text: Having spokes diverging from centre of gunnery clock-face

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunnery arm
the face of a clock is its dial

explanation.surface: A description of lines spreading out from the middle of an artillery clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre' tempts you to take a middle letter of 'gunnery', but it belongs to the definition; 'of' only links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel whose spokes spread out from a hub is the textbook example of a radial arrangement.

clue.text: Tanks having water and fresh air

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters are made anew in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Containers holding water and clean air.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria are glass tanks for keeping fish and other water creatures.

clue.text: Start what I did in restaurant

parts.note: taken as written
it stands for the restaurant just mentioned
what I did in a restaurant was eat: I ate

explanation.surface: Someone recounts what they did at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is read as a phrase: 'it' stands for the restaurant, and what I did there was eat, so the words run together as 'in it I ate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to begin it or set it going.

clue.text: Three-quarters of learned people having lines from books

indicators.note: three-quarters of says only six of the eight letters are kept, the last two dropped

parts.note: the literati are well-read, educated people
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: Educated people who quote passages from books.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary describes what concerns or comes from books and written works.

clue.text: She heard about it having been used again

indicators.note: about means the letters are scattered around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has heard an item of gossip that is being recycled.
explanation.definitionFit: Old material served up once more in a new form is said to be rehashed, as with stale news.

clue.text: Heroine's false statement in project

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to project is to stick out, to jut
a false statement is a lie

explanation.surface: A heroine tells an untruth while working on some project.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Heroine' is read as 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Juliet, beloved of Romeo, is one of the best-known heroines in drama.

clue.text: Go long way with artist first in medley

parts.note: far means a long way off
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to travel a great distance with a painter leading, through a mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' moves the artist ahead of 'Go', though the clue prints them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture or jumble of things, much as a medley is.

clue.text: One fights naked over South American city, right?

indicators.note: over in a down-the-page sense signals the word for naked is turned backwards

parts.note: raw can mean bare or naked, as in 'in the raw'
Rio de Janeiro is the Brazilian city usually shortened to Rio

explanation.surface: A question about whether a naked fighter has crossed a South American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrior is a soldier or fighter, someone whose role is to do battle.

clue.text: Spray gun

parts.note: a toy firearm that squirts a jet of liquid rather than paint

explanation.walkthrough: A spray gun is normally a decorator's paint tool; here it is the child's toy that squirts liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's toy that shoots jets of liquid is literally a gun that sprays.

clue.text: Health-giver?

parts.note: to drink someone's health is to toast them, and the person who leads the toasts at a formal dinner gives the healths

explanation.walkthrough: 'Health-giver' suggests a doctor or a tonic, but 'health' here is a toast drunk at a banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: At a formal banquet the official who announces speakers and proposes toasts calls on guests to drink healths.

clue.text: Put into liquidation?

parts.note: liquidation suggests a bankrupt firm, but is read as put into liquid

explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquidation' looks like a business winding-up; read it as placed in liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dunked or plunged into a fluid has been submerged under it.

clue.text: Interruption long time afterwards causing damage

parts.note: a break is an interruption
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A pause long ago leads to some harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afterwards' places the long time after the interruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakage means damage caused by things being broken, as in a shop's charge for breakages.

clue.text: Alarm artist about methods of self-defence

indicators.note: about here means the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter gets a fright and turns to learning how to protect themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo, karate and kung fu are combat disciplines taught as ways of defending oneself.

clue.text: Meddle with tuner I'd repaired

indicators.note: repaired suggests the letters are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone interferes with a tuner they had mended.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to butt in or interfere where not wanted.

clue.text: Fit and size fancy furrier occasionally missed

indicators.note: fancy implies the letters are rearranged in an elaborate way
occasionally missed means every other letter of the word is skipped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A furrier is caught out over the fitting and sizing of a fancy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A seizure is a sudden attack or fit, as in an epileptic fit.

clue.text: Husband in drab boat

indicators.note: in says one letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: dingy means drab or dull

explanation.surface: A husband sitting in a dull little vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small open boat, often a tender to a larger vessel.

clue.text: Threaten to come to a devilish conclusion

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: A warning of an approaching hellish finish.
explanation.definitionFit: When something looms or is about to happen, menacingly, it is said to be imminent in this way.

clue.text: One who used to play Shylock, say

definitions.meaning: split as ..., a former performer, someone who once acted on stage
Shylock, the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice, demands his pound of flesh, an example of one who insists on payment

explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites reading 'Shylock' as a part once played; instead he is the second definition, the moneylender who demands his pound of flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Shylock insists on his bond being paid in full, the very picture of someone demanding what is owed.

clue.text: Heavy metal, one that's strange, I had one inside

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: inside says these letters go within the word for strange

parts.note: rum is a British informal word for odd or strange
I'd is the contraction of I had
one again gives the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A heavy-metal fan admits to having an odd musical taste.
explanation.definitionFit: This element of the platinum group is among the densest metals known, so it is truly heavy.

clue.text: Friends turned up with lots of good food to eat served in style

definitions.text: with lots of good food to eat served in style

indicators.note: turned means the word for friends is spun round to read backwards

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: Friends arrive for a lavish feast with plenty to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a British informal term for a lavish, generous spread of food.

clue.text: Fight to include part of best rug gleaming

indicators.note: to include part of says the answer is held within a run of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A battle over a shining prize rug.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Fight to include' as the definition; the definition is 'Fight' alone, and 'to include part of' tells us the answer lies within 'best rug gleaming'.
explanation.definitionFit: A struggle is a fight or tussle, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Train passes by the European

parts.note: to pass away is to die, so passes gives dies
el is the word for 'the' in Spanish, a European language

explanation.surface: A train goes past a European.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a locomotive or train powered by a diesel engine.

clue.text: Sportsman regarded as favourite

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University
eyed means looked at, regarded

explanation.surface: An athlete is considered the top pick.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is someone who has played for Oxford or Cambridge University against the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The blue-eyed boy is an idiom for the favoured one, someone's pet.
